name: Jack Pierse

education.notes: UCD graduate in accounting per Acuity magazine / Crunchbase / Business Post coverage. Exact years not disclosed publicly; assuming standard 3–4 year programme ending around 2013–2014 given a 1992 birth year.
ACA via Chartered Accountants Ireland, trained at PwC Dublin (graduate programme).

keyDecisions: Took the PwC Dublin graduate programme straight out of UCD to qualify as a Chartered Accountant (ACA) — a structured 3-ish year apprenticeship rather than going direct into a startup or VC.
Chose audit-track financial rigour as a foundation rather than chasing a brand-name finance job in London immediately.
lessons: ACA training at a Big Four is a rare combination: it pays you to learn financial-statement literacy, it ages you into rooms with CFOs, and it ports anywhere in the world.
In Ireland the ACA → fintech founder path is now well-trodden; the qualification is closer to an MBA-equivalent in credential weight than people outside Ireland realise.
careerSteps.notes: Confirmed PwC Dublin graduate / chartered accountant per multiple sources (Acuity, Crunchbase, Barden). Exact start year not disclosed; consistent with c.2013–2017 for a 1992-born UCD grad.

careerSteps.company: Highway1 (San Francisco hardware accelerator) and others
keyDecisions: Post-ACA, took venture-adjacent roles (including Highway1 — PCH's hardware accelerator in SF) rather than staying on the audit / finance track.
Used the venture-side stint to build the network and pattern-recognition that fed directly into Wayflyer.
lessons: ACA → VC-adjacent operator is a high-leverage pivot: you arrive with financial credibility AND get founder pattern matching.
Even a short stint inside an accelerator is enough to learn the shape of a fundraise from the other side of the table.
careerSteps.notes: Per Crunchbase / TechCrunch, Pierse worked at Highway1 (the SF-based hardware accelerator run by PCH) before Wayflyer. researchLinks specifically references the TechCrunch Highway1 tag. Exact tenure dates not disclosed.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Wayflyer (revenue-based financing for e-commerce) with Aidan Corbett in 2019 — Pierse came up with the original idea.
Took the CFO seat rather than CEO — clean split with a commercial CEO co-founder.

Rode the 2020–2021 e-commerce / COVID tailwind aggressively, scaling capital deployment via debt facilities (Left Lane $76M Series A May 2021; DST $150M Series B Feb 2022 at >$1.6B valuation; JPMorgan $300M debt May 2022).
Departed Wayflyer in July 2023 at peak rather than coasting — chose another founding cycle over a CFO sinecure.
lessons: ACA-trained CFO + commercial CEO is a defensible role split for a fintech — regulators, banks and LPs all expect a real numbers person.
Macro tailwinds compress timelines — Wayflyer reached unicorn status in roughly 29 months.
A first unicorn doesn't have to be a destination; some founders treat them as a learning lap.
careerSteps.notes: Wayflyer reached $1.6B+ valuation in Feb 2022; 2023 revenue €62.5M, 2024 €95.2M. Pierse held Co-Founder & CFO, later titled Co-Founder & President (Inventory Sourcing) before departing July 2023.

keyDecisions: Began angel investing while still operating at Wayflyer — backed US fintech Arc's Series A (~$20M).
Concentrated picks in fintech where his ACA + Wayflyer pattern recognition is highest-signal.
lessons: Operator-investor overlap accelerates network density and dealflow.
Angel investing while still operating is a legitimate way to start a track record before going full-time investor.
careerSteps.notes: Public reporting links him to Arc's ~$20M Series A among other fintech bets.

keyDecisions: Launched HappyStack — Dublin-based e-commerce intelligence / software solutions — as his second founding rather than going full-time investor.
Also launched an internship programme aimed at developing 1,000 new entrepreneurs — invests in the Irish founder funnel itself.
lessons: A second venture can be smaller-stack and more software-flavoured than the first — capital-heavy fintech is not the only viable path once you have liquidity.
Ireland is a viable founding base for back-to-back ventures; domicile is not the bottleneck.
careerSteps.notes: HappyStack referenced in researchLinks (happystack.com) and confirmed via Silicon Republic coverage.

outcomes.currentStatus: Departed Wayflyer in July 2023. Building HappyStack (Dublin, e-commerce intelligence) and active angel investor in fintech.

lessons.lesson: UCD accounting → PwC Dublin ACA → VC-adjacent operator (Highway1) → fintech CFO co-founder is one of the cleanest Irish-founder ladders of the 2010s–2020s.
lessons.source: Synthesised from Acuity, Crunchbase, Silicon Republic and Business Post coverage.

lessons.lesson: Accountant-rigor + adjacency to capital markets unlocks a novel financing product when a wave (e-commerce, COVID) hits.
Co-founder role specialisation (commercial CEO + finance CFO) is a defensible structure for regulated / financial products.
Ireland is a viable founding base for global fintech — domicile is not the bottleneck.
